entries.clue: A wander back before ten score slowly (6)

indicators.note: 'back' means in the reverse direction, so the word for wander is read from its end to its start
'before' puts the A and DAG ahead of IO in the answer

blocks.note: IO looks like the digits of 10

annotation.surface: Someone ambling along and totting up a score at a leisurely pace.
annotation.walkthrough: Adagio is the Italian marking written in a musical score telling players to go slowly, so 'score slowly' is the definition; 'score' is not about points.
annotation.definitionFit: Adagio is the tempo instruction printed in a score meaning slowly.

entries.clue: Ray's direction could be optional (13)

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

annotation.surface: Someone called Ray finds that following his instructions is up to you.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole thirteen-letter fodder is sitting in the first two words; the apostrophe is ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: Something discretionary is left to your choice, so optional.

entries.clue: Given bribes as overcome by avarice (7)

indicators.note: AS is covered over by GREED, which surrounds it

blocks.note: kept as it stands, placed inside

annotation.surface: A tale of officials taking backhanders because greed got the better of them.
annotation.walkthrough: To grease someone's palm is to bribe them, so 'greased' works as 'given bribes'.
annotation.definitionFit: Greasing a palm is slang for bribing, so greased means given bribes.

entries.clue: Because of overgrowing toadstools (5,2)

indicators.note: the answer grows inside the words that follow, covered over by the letters around it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: An excuse blamed on toadstools taking over the garden.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words, which is what hides it.
annotation.definitionFit: Owing to and because of both introduce a cause.

entries.clue: Reserve player is expected to conquer (6)

blocks.note: a sub is a substitute on the bench
due = expected, as in 'the train is due'

annotation.surface: A substitute coming on is predicted to win the match.
annotation.walkthrough: The sporting surface makes 'conquer' look like part of the match report rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to conquer a people or an enemy is to bring them under control.

entries.clue: Son, alas, ruined sauce (5)

indicators.note: ALAS is wrecked into a new order

annotation.surface: A parent laments that their son has spoiled the sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen disaster in the surface is real, but only 'alas' is ruined.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the word is Spanish for sauce, and in English names a spicy tomato one.

entries.clue: Sandy stretch with tree, we hear (5)

indicators.note: the answer is how 'beech' sounds when spoken

annotation.surface: A sandy shore with a single tree on it.
annotation.walkthrough: Beech and beach are pronounced identically.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the sand along a shore is exactly the stretch the answer covers.

entries.clue: Current theme put in, out perhaps (2,2,3,6)

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged differently

annotation.surface: Someone debating whether to include a subject in a piece of writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like electricity or water flow, but it means modern; 'in' and 'out' look like instructions and are only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Up to the minute means completely current, bang up to date.

entries.clue: Extraordinary, astonishing eclipse around first of August (8)

indicators.note: ECLIPSE is stunned out of shape
the rearranged letters go round A
take only the opening letter of August

blocks.note: the first letter of August, placed inside

annotation.surface: An eclipse at the start of August, described as amazing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' and 'astonishing' sit side by side like a pair of synonyms, but only the first is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional or out of the ordinary.

entries.clue: Neat sort of stake (4)

indicators.note: a kind of version of NEAT, its letters reordered

annotation.surface: A tidy kind of wager.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as an adjective describing the stake; it is only the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each poker player puts in before the deal.

entries.clue: Star turn for ballet, painting etc (4)

indicators.note: a turn is a change of course, so the letters of STAR take a new order

annotation.surface: A leading performer's turn at a variety show of dance and art.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star turn' is a stock phrase for a headline act, which hides that 'turn' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: ballet and painting are two members of the class, and 'etc' signals that the list stands for the whole.

entries.clue: Fruit filled with successful form of carbon (8)

indicators.note: GRAPE has HIT stuffed inside it

blocks.note: a grape is a fruit, the outer piece
a hit is a success, placed inside

annotation.surface: A piece of fruit stuffed with some chemical element.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Successful' is an adjective and HIT a noun, but a hit show is a successful one, so the swap is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Graphite is a soft crystalline form of carbon, the 'lead' in pencils.

entries.clue: Street of sound, not a TV room (6)

indicators.note: the A is left out of AUDIO

annotation.surface: A road known for its music, with no room for television.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not a TV room' reads as a denial, but 'not a' belongs to the wordplay and 'TV room' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific sense: the room where programmes are filmed and broadcast, as in 'back to the studio'.

entries.clue: He'd captured member and caused injury (6)

indicators.note: HED takes ARM prisoner, holding it inside

blocks.note: the apostrophe dropped, the outer piece
an arm is a limb, or member, placed inside

annotation.surface: A man seized someone's limb and hurt them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' in crosswords is often a limb; here the arm is both the captive and the wound.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: having caused injury to someone is having hurt them.

entries.clue: Worker observed tool (7)

blocks.note: a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand

annotation.surface: A labourer spotted a tool lying about.
annotation.walkthrough: SAW looks like the tool itself, but here it is the past tense of see.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a one-handed saw for cutting wood belongs to the broad class of carpentry tools.

entries.clue: Witty responses about legal wrongs (7)

blocks.note: re = about, as in memo headers
a tort is a civil wrong in law

annotation.surface: Clever comebacks traded in a dispute over civil lawsuits.
annotation.walkthrough: A tort is the legal term for a wrong that can be sued over, such as negligence or trespass.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sharp, clever comebacks thrown back in an argument.

entries.clue: Transformation of aunt in spring (8)

indicators.note: the letters are transformed into a new order

annotation.surface: An aunt has a makeover when the new season arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' and 'in' look like link words but are part of the fodder; 'spring' is water, not the season.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: a natural source of water welling up was called this long before the ornamental jet in a square.

entries.clue: Idea I rejected as unacceptable (3,2)

indicators.note: the I is thrown out of NOTION

annotation.surface: A proposal of mine was turned down for being out of order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is British informal speech for something that should not be allowed: 'That's just not on.'
annotation.definitionFit: In British speech, something that is not on is unacceptable.

entries.clue: Where maps are finally cut short (5)

indicators.note: the last letter of AT LAST is lopped off

blocks.note: AT LAST minus its final T

annotation.surface: A question about where maps have ended up being trimmed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally' tempts you to take a last letter, but it is a whole phrase, AT LAST, which then loses its tail.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-style description: a bound book of maps is the place maps are to be found.

entries.clue: The one just here in ancient history (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the last of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: Pointing at one particular item in a study of the ancient past.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, taking the final T of 'ancient'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'This' names the thing right here, as opposed to 'that'.

entries.clue: Time to behave with discretion (4)

annotation.surface: Advice that it is the moment to conduct yourself carefully.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single instruction, hiding the split after 'behave'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe skill in handling delicate matters without giving offence.

entries.clue: Glowing desire turns sour (8)

indicators.note: SOUR is turned into a new order

annotation.surface: A burning passion that goes bad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glowing desire' reads as one phrase, a passion, but 'Glowing' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something with a soft shining sheen, like pearls or silk, seems to glow.

entries.clue: Holds inner longing for animals (6)

indicators.note: YEN goes on the inside of HAS

blocks.note: a yen is a longing, placed inside

annotation.surface: Someone harbours a secret craving for creatures.
annotation.walkthrough: Yen for a longing is informal English, borrowed from Chinese, not the Japanese currency.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: these African scavenging mammals are covered by the broad class 'animals'.

entries.clue: Ring for cleaner (6)

blocks.note: the flat metal ring slipped under a nut or bolt
one who, or a machine that, cleans things with water

annotation.surface: Phoning a cleaner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb, to phone, but it is the noun, the metal disc with a hole.
annotation.definitionFit: A washer is both a flat ring and something that cleans.
